title: It’s a Tool Not a Crutch: A Pilot Generative AI Intervention to Enhance Pre-service Teachers’ Self-efficacy and AI Literacy
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether a generative AI-supported scenario-based learning (SBL) intervention can improve pre-service teachers’ self-efficacy and AI literacy. The study is motivated by the rapid uptake of GenAI tools in education and the need to understand both their pedagogical value and their risks, especially in teacher education. The authors frame the work around the question of how GenAI can be integrated into initial teacher education (ITE) in ways that are educationally useful, ethically responsible, and developmentally appropriate.

The intervention used Microsoft CoPilot in two two-hour workshops. In the first workshop, participants completed structured scenario tasks where CoPilot generated classroom vignettes aligned with self-efficacy dimensions such as instructional strategies, classroom management, and student engagement, along with response options and feedback. In the second, participants reflected on a dilemma from school placement and dialogued with CoPilot in a more open-ended way. The study used pre/post survey measures of teacher self-efficacy and AI literacy, plus focus groups with primary pre-service teachers. Participants came from an Irish university context and included 4th-year undergraduate primary pre-service teachers and 2nd-year postgraduate post-primary pre-service teachers.

Findings suggest the intervention increased self-efficacy and AI literacy, especially awareness, usage, and evaluation of AI. Qualitative data showed participants valued the low-stakes scenario practice, immediate feedback, and opportunities for reflection. At the same time, the paper highlights important limitations and risks, including overreliance on AI, the need for critical evaluation of outputs, concerns about trustworthiness, and the importance of scaffolding for early-stage trainees. The authors conclude that GenAI can function as a supportive pedagogical tool in ITE, but only if embedded thoughtfully, with attention to ethics, developmental stage, and long-term impact.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI chatbot/assistant used to generate, adapt, and provide feedback on scenario-based learning prompts and responses.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as Microsoft CoPilot in a pilot scenario-based learning intervention to generate classroom scenarios, offer multiple response options, provide feedback, and suggest readings for pre-service teachers.

findings.finding_summary: In this pilot mixed-methods study with pre-service teachers (primary n=12; post-primary n=6; total n=18), the GenAI-SBL intervention increased overall teacher self-efficacy from a mean of 74 to 80.35. Subscale means also increased for instructional strategies (25.71 to 27.35), classroom management (24.82 to 27.12), and student engagement (23.47 to 25.88).
findings.measure: Teacher self-efficacy scale (overall and subscales: instructional strategies, classroom management, student engagement)

findings.finding_summary: AI literacy scores improved after the intervention, with overall AI literacy rising from 51.12 to 62.23. Subscale means increased for AI awareness (13.59 to 15.18), AI usage (12.29 to 15.76), AI evaluation (11.88 to 16.88), and AI ethics (13.55 to 14.41).
findings.measure: AI literacy scale (overall and subscales: awareness, usage, evaluation, ethics)

quality_tier_rationale: This is an exploratory mixed-methods pilot study with a very small sample and no control group, so it provides limited causal evidence. The design is informative but not strong enough for a higher evidence tier.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported gains are positive but small-scale and descriptive, with no effect sizes reported. Impact is therefore promising but uncertain and not yet established at medium or large magnitude.
